title: Mission Scenario 3: High-Altitude Hohmann Transfer
learning_goals: Insert vehicle into initial 200 km LEO parking orbit.
Compute velocity increments Delta-V_1 and Delta-V_2 using the vis-viva equation.
Execute two-burn Hohmann transfer to Geostationary Orbit (35,786 km GEO).

rules.text: Flight computer checklist and guidance diagnostics must be run prior to launch.
rules.hint: Execute preflight avionics and telemetry checklist before clearance requests.

rules.text: Propellant load must not be empty or exceed maximum certified tank capacity.
rules.hint: Load propellant within maximum structural capacity of tank stages.

rules.text: Liftoff thrust-to-weight ratio must exceed 1.0 (TWR > 1.0) to achieve positive climb acceleration.
rules.hint: Maintain liftoff Thrust-to-Weight Ratio above 1.15 to clear launch pad.

rules.text: Payload mass must be formally declared and within upper stage structural limits.
rules.hint: Ensure payload mass remains strictly within launch vehicle LEO insertion limits.

rules.text: Lower booster stage burnout required before staging separation and upper stage ignition.
rules.hint: Separate depleted booster stage only after complete engine burnout.

rules.text: Range safety radar tracking and downrange airspace clearance required before ignition.
rules.hint: Obtain positive range safety tracking clearance prior to main engine ignition.

rules.text: Trajectory budget must maintain at least a 5% delta-v reserve margin to avoid orbital decay.
rules.hint: Achieve minimum orbital delta-v budget (9.3 km/s) for stable orbital insertion.

rules.text: Telemetry review and flight debrief must be completed before submitting final flight report.
rules.hint: Debrief flight computer telemetry before generating final mission report.

choose_rocket: High-altitude transfers require a multi-stage heavy lift vehicle.
Orbis Heavy features a high-energy transfer stage with 420s vacuum ISP.
Select Orbis Heavy to provide the required ~13.5 km/s total Delta-V capability.
declare_payload: Geostationary communications satellites require significant structural mass.
Declare a 1,000 kg communications satellite for high-orbit transfer.
Set payload mass to 1,000 kg on the payload console.
fuel_rocket: Full propellant load is mandatory for multi-burn geostationary transfer.
The two Hohmann burns require substantial upper-stage propellant reserve.
Fill all stages to 100% capacity (fuel ratio 1.0).
run_checklist: Run avionics and multi-restart upper stage guidance diagnostics.
Checklist validates restart capabilities for the transfer and circularization burns.
clear_range: Downrange deep-space tracking stations must confirm tracking acquisition.
Clear range safety with the tracking console.
launch: Ignite core booster to achieve 200 km LEO parking orbit.
Ascent trajectory delivers upper stage to perigee of transfer ellipse.
Launch vehicle to initial low Earth orbit.
coast: Coast in parking orbit until reaching the optimal transfer burn node.
Perigee ignition provides maximum Oberth effect efficiency.
Coast to equatorial ascending node for transfer burn.
burn_transfer: Execute first Hohmann burn Delta-V_1 (~2,450 m/s) to raise apogee to 35,786 km.
Vis-viva equation dictates velocity increase into the elliptical transfer orbit.
Command Hohmann transfer burn from the flight computer.
circularize: Execute second burn Delta-V_2 (~1,480 m/s) at apogee to circularize orbit.
Circularization eliminates orbital eccentricity, stabilizing the GEO orbit.
debrief: Verify final circular orbit at 35,786 km with near-zero eccentricity.
Check Keplerian orbital period (~86,164s) matching Earth sidereal rotation.
Debrief flight telemetry to complete the mission.

common_mistakes.remedy: Obtain range safety clearance and run preflight checklist before ignition.
Ensure booster stage thrust exceeds total wet vehicle weight (TWR > 1.0).
